evidence.title: Incident Report: Toronto Transit-Grid Cyberattack
evidence.content: A cyberattack on Toronto's transit-grid operator was publicly attributed to a state actor. Ally investigator Agent Priya Chandran shared the attack payload with HER STORY before the public attribution went final.

evidence.title: Agent Priya Chandran: Shared Case Notes
evidence.content: "Everyone upstairs wants to name the state actor and move on. Something about the payload signature bothers me. I'd rather be slow and right."

evidence.title: Attack Payload — Registry Match
evidence.content: Hash Compare returns a third confirmed hit on the same toolkit family logged in Cases 001, 005, and 007. This attack was not state-sponsored — it was staged by Corvid/LOOM operatives.

evidence.title: Recovered LOOM Internal Memo
evidence.content:
LOOM INTERNAL — FIELD CALIBRATION LOG

Cases catalogued 001 through 007, logged as "field calibration runs." Notation: "Investigator response patterns nominal. Continue observation."

The player's own solved cases are logged here as data used to refine what LOOM could get away with.

evidence.title: Emergency Infrastructure-Access Legislation Draft
evidence.content: Proposed emergency legislation granting LOOM-class predictive systems privileged infrastructure access, filed in the days immediately following the attack. See Timeline for the exact date gap.

chat.text: I found our intake logs. Someone's been suggesting which cases get routed to you. I don't think all of those calls were mine.

suspects.notes: Third confirmed toolkit hash match. Attack staged to justify emergency legislation granting LOOM-class systems infrastructure access.

solution.successMessage: Third hit on the same hash, same family, same hands. The state actor didn't do this — Corvid did, and the timing proves why: an attack, then six days later, a bill asking for exactly the access this attack made urgent. Chandran's instinct to be slow and right was correct.
